notes: Colloquial masculine تعبان (ta'ban) agrees with the speaker; feminine تعبانة (Levantine ta'bane). Form shared across Levantine, Egyptian, Gulf and Iraqi Arabic (MSA uses متعب).
Colloquial masculine جوعان (ju'an); feminine جوعانة (ju'ane). Widespread in Levantine and other dialects; the fa'lan adjective pattern also exists in Classical Arabic.
Colloquial masculine مبسوط (mabsut); feminine مبسوطة (mabsuta). Common to Levantine and Egyptian Arabic.
Colloquial feminine تعبانة (Levantine ta'bane) agrees with the speaker; masculine تعبان (ta'ban).
Feminine تعبانة agrees with the third-person subject هي (she), not the speaker; the speaker's gender is unknown.

glossEn: Where are you going? (asked of a woman)
notes: Feminine active participle رايحة marks the ADDRESSEE, not the speaker (masculine addressee: وين رايح؟); وين is Levantine 'where'.
